The slice finished cleanly — here's what it says:

* Print time: about 54 minutes
* Filament: 26.5 g of PLA, roughly $0.66
* Your strength changes are all in it (4 walls, 40% gyroid infill, 4 bottom layers), and all three pieces get a brim, which helps them hold on to the plate.

Orca did flag two things I want you to decide on, because they're about the design, not the settings:

1. The three pieces overlap. The arrow (root_1) and both arcs sit in each other's space, so Orca warns that collisions may be caused. If the emblem is meant to be one solid part, they should be joined into a single object (I can do that — one undo step). If instead they are separate parts that only look nested in the top view, they need to be moved apart before printing.
2. root_1 has "floating regions" — areas with nothing directly underneath that Orca suggests supporting or re-orienting away. Nothing is actually printed in mid-air, so the print will finish; the risk is those undersides sagging or curling a little rather than the print failing.

I haven't sent anything to the printer — you press Send when you're ready.
Merge them into oneAdd supports
</pasted_content id="22cb">

agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:5:JusPrin replaces what OrcaSlicer looks like and how people move through it. It keeps everything OrcaSlicer already does well to turn a model into a print. agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:21:Prepare is the screen people stay on. **Check print** opens a modal window. OrcaSlicer's original Preview stays where it was, in `Plater`'s Notebook (OrcaSlicer's tabbed container). A small factory function on `Plater`, with nothing JusPrin-specific in it, gives that window the existing model, bed, slicing process, and G-code result. Closing the window returns focus to Prepare. The window also closes by itself when the project or the slice changes. **Print** currently opens OrcaSlicer's existing send confirmation dialog. It never sends straight away. agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:123:`Shell/GcodeHistoryRecorder` writes the records where OrcaSlicer already says a file left: `EVT_OUTPUT_EXPORTED` for an export (OrcaSlicer's own and the `export_file` tool's), the Bambu print and send jobs' finished events while their dialog is showing, and the print-host queue's enqueue observer followed by the queue dialog's progress at 100. Each time, a copy of the G-code is kept at `<project>/gcode/<hash>.gcode` (the last `kKeptGcodeCopies` per project). It polls Bambu printers every two seconds whatever is on screen; `Agent/PrintOutcomeTracker` decides which report belongs to which send, and a finish of a project that is not open is written into that project's saved document. Print-host printers record sends only. The model reads the last ten records as `printHistory` in its workspace block.
agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:125:The records are shown on one screen, Print history, the second screen of the Home page (`HomeUI/src/components/PrintHistory.tsx`). It is a leaf of Home and of the project: the gallery's header link, a project card's or printer card's history line, the project pane's Print history row and a chat marker's "history" link all open it, and where it was opened from sets its first filter. Back from the gallery stays in the page; opened from the project, the shell selects Home with the screen named (`ShellController::open_print_history`, sent as the `screen` message when Home comes on screen) and Back selects the tab it came from. The page asks for the entries (`history_request`) each time it opens and each time the host's state moves under it; `Home/PrintHistory` builds them from every project's records, pure and tested in `agent_bridge_tests`, with what only the application knows (preset labels, which printer card a printer is, the exported files' checks) passed in by `OrcaHomeBackend`. An exported file is hashed again when the screen asks, unless its size and time are as they were at the last hash. Export… writes the project's kept copy and records it; Export again on a changed file writes a new file beside it. Open in chat opens the project if another is open and asks the Agent page to show the chat and scroll to the marker (`reveal_item`). The page phrases every line; nothing records, badges or draws a failure.
agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:127:Print again sends a recorded G-code's kept file, never a fresh slice, and always through OrcaSlicer's own send dialog, where the person presses Send. A Bambu printer takes a `.gcode.3mf`, so a Bambu print also keeps the package it uploaded (`<hash>.gcode.3mf`, and for a cloud printer the config 3MF it also sent), byte for byte, with its SHA-256 on the send (`packageHash`); it goes when its G-code's copy is pruned. Print again parses that package, hands it to Select Machine through `Plater::update_print_required_data` and `EVT_PRINT_FROM_SDCARD_VIEW` (the printer file browser's print-from-storage mode, which draws the plate, picture and filaments from the file), and sets the dialog's new-print flag (`SelectMachineDialog::set_required_data_new_print`, the one upstream seam), so the job uploads the local file as a new print instead of asking the printer to print by name. Printing from the printer's storage is not used: the file name on the printer is reused per project, so it cannot say which version would print. A print host with OrcaSlicer's standard upload dialog is sent a temporary copy of the kept G-code (the queue deletes what it uploads); ElegooLink, Creality Print, Flashforge's local API and `use_3mf` hosts are not offered Print again. `GcodeHistoryRecorder::print_again_state` decides whether it is offered for the printer selected now; a kept file whose hash no longer matches is never sent and the entry says so. `print_dialog_open` opens the same dialogs for the agent: a plate's slice, or with `gcode` a recorded G-code.

agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:144:- A model file never silently lands in whatever project happened to be open behind Home. Before 2026-10-24 Home's Import button did exactly that, because it called OrcaSlicer's `add_model`, and from 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-28 the most recent project reopened behind Home at startup. Home now starts with a blank project behind it, but whatever is open there is still not where a file opened from Home goes.
agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:152:**Finding the way to add a part.** With Home's button named Open, the person who wants a second part in the project they have needs to find it from Prepare. Every slicer solves this the same way, with a control inside the workspace that is always on screen: PrusaSlicer's Add button on the top toolbar and Cmd+I, Cura's folder icon at the top left of Prepare, and OrcaSlicer's own Add button on the main toolbar, which JusPrin hides. Dragging onto the plate is in addition to that control in all three, never the only way. JusPrin keeps the same shape: a **+ Add model** button under the plate list in the Plates tab of the Plates and Project pane, drawn like **+ Add plate** and placed directly above it, so the two things that can be added there sit together with the commoner one first (chosen on 2026-10-24 from a drawn comparison against a plus in the tab header and a row under the open plate), plus File › Import (Cmd+I), the composer's + menu, and the empty plate's hint ("Drop a model here or add one"). A person who asks the agent to add a file gets it added as well.
agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:158:- The shell's handler (`ShellController::take_opened_files`) leaves a .3mf to OrcaSlicer, which opens it as a project through `load_project` and so asks the "Previously opened file" question; files given with it are added to that project. Any other files are opened in a new project named after the first one: the open project is saved and released the way the agent's `project_open` releases it, then OrcaSlicer's own load runs into the new project, and the app goes to Prepare.
agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:160:- File › Import › Import Zip Archive also reaches `load_files(wxArrayString)`, so a zip on its own keeps OrcaSlicer's behavior and adds. Home's Open… and a drop on Home open a zip in a new project like any model file.
agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:163:- A 3MF saved for another printer keeps that printer: OrcaSlicer selects the file's system printer profile (a P1S, say) and draws its bed, the person's own printer is not re-selected, and the file's process and filament settings stay as the designer saved them. The header's printer chip is marked "from the file" while the selected profile is not a named printer (decided 2026-10-28, see the design system's Header chip); the agent's load report carries the change (`selectedSetupChange.printerPreset`) and its first message asks which printer to use. OrcaSlicer's "sync the printer information?" question is answered No on every open, since the app stores that answer at startup.
agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:173:| `PrintIssues/NoticeKinds` | Where each of OrcaSlicer's notification kinds goes: the issue list, a confirmation, running work, application state, or nowhere. Every kind is named; a kind OrcaSlicer adds stops the build in this file until someone routes it. |
agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:188:- **No pill is the all-clear, and it is never given before a check.** The pill is drawn only while OrcaSlicer reports an issue, ignored ones included. While OrcaSlicer holds an unapplied edit the last issues are kept, the pill says it is checking and both buttons are off, so the pill does not go until OrcaSlicer has looked. An issue that was not in the list before is announced once by a ring that spreads from the pill twice; an edit that keeps an issue, and ignoring one or undoing that, announce nothing.
agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:189:- **Nothing is resolved by the fork.** An issue goes when OrcaSlicer lets go of its notification. An agent saying it fixed something changes nothing.
agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:193:- **Slice-result warnings follow OrcaSlicer's send dialog.** The warnings the G-code processor stores on a slice result (bed temperature, nozzle hardness, timelapse) are shown as OrcaSlicer's Bambu send dialog shows them, the only place OrcaSlicer itself shows them: never the bed-temperature one, the traditional-timelapse one once although it is stored twice. The chip and `slice_report` read one fork-owned table, `Workspace/SliceResultWarnings`, whose comment says why it is a copy and not an upstream seam, and a guard test fails when OrcaSlicer defines a kind the table does not classify. The timelapse ones apply only to a print that records a timelapse, which is chosen when it is sent: `slice_report` and Check print list them marked so, and the chip does not count them.
agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:217:- **It reads or changes OrcaSlicer state:** presets, the model, plates, slicing, the device list. The page never owns project state (see the constraints below).
agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:258:Semantic annotations are labels a person puts on part of a model to say what that part means, such as a face that must stay smooth. Reuse what OrcaSlicer's painting tools already do: raycasting, brush selection, clipping, showing painted facets, copying, undo, and saving into the 3MF file. Two things are not yet proven for production: labels with arbitrary meanings, and how those labels are presented to the agent. The first implementation should use two labels on one object. Before adding more labels, check that those two survive save and reload, transforms, duplication, undo and redo, and changes to the mesh's topology.
agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md:148:- Setup card (the design system's `PinnedSetupCard`; the "JusPrin v2" canvas, page "Current Setup Card", decided 2026-10-26): the band docked under the chat header, the one place in the Agent pane that is always now. Two parts. Above a 1 DIP `border.subtle` rule, the words someone wrote: the person's purpose in Body Bold, wrapping to two lines and then clipped (the whole of it in the tooltip), and the agent's plan headline in Body Small, `text.primary`; each is present only once written, and with neither the section and its rule are absent, with nothing standing in for them (not the preset name, not the project name, not a hint). Below the rule, OrcaSlicer's facts: the process and first filament presets with "N settings changed" (the project's differences from the presets and the objects' own settings) in Body Small, `text.secondary`, wrapping to two lines and then clipped like the purpose (decided 2026-10-26: at the pane's default width a Bambu preset name with a count overflows one line), and the "All settings" Button/Link, in Body Small Bold, on its first line's baseline; then the time, material and plate figures in Body Small Bold, or the one line that stands in for them ("Not sliced yet" with a Compute estimates link, "Time & material estimates recomputing…"). The eyebrow is "Setup summary" in Label Bold, `action.primary`; the only state beside it is "Agent working". A saved chat's card is the same card in `text.secondary` with the eyebrow "Earlier setup" or "Saved sliced snapshot", a quiet state such as "Saved Oct 3, 10:42" and a footnote line.
agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md:152:- All settings panel (the "JusPrin v2" canvas, page "Current Setup Card", the four "All settings" boards): opened from the "All settings" link at the end of the setup card's presets line, it takes the Agent pane's place under a header of the compact icon button back to the chat, the title in Body Bold and the pane's own toggle. A "Showing" row holds the design system's Select (`component.select`: 26 DIP, `small` radius, Body text, a 16 DIP chevron, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` stroke that strengthens on hover and becomes the focus ring when open; its menu is the Menu/Popover under its left edge, as wide as the field) listing the whole project, each plate when there are two or more, and each object; it follows the selection in the 3D view. Under it a Field/Search ("Search settings") beside an All / Changed Segmented Control. The presets in use sit in a `surface.subtle` box with the `medium` radius, each filament slot with its Swatch (`component.swatch`, 24 DIP, `small` radius, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` inside stroke). Groups are OrcaSlicer's own pages (Quality, Strength, Speed, Support, Multimaterial, Others, then Filament and Printer) with a 32 DIP header row (16 DIP chevron, Body Small Bold name, Label summary at the right) and rows indented 24 DIP: Body Small name and value on a 28 DIP line, a changed value in Body Small Bold with "Preset: …" in Metadata under it. Two or three filament slots stand side by side, one column per slot; more than three go through a slot picker, one at a time. The host reads the whole table in one message (`settings_catalog`, the `all_settings` capability). Only one object's view has anything to press: a Button/Link at the end of a row's note, under the value, where the table marks one — "Use project value" under a setting the object, a part, a modifier or a height range sets itself (not a range's own layer height or filament, which define it), and "Remove" under its support blockers or enforcers. Each press is one OrcaSlicer undo step of the person's, named for what it did, and the panel redraws from the host's next table (`settings_action`, the `settings_actions` capability).
agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md:165:- Header chip: 28 DIP high, `chip` radius (`component.chip`). The chip states the selection: the printer profile the project will be sliced for, its nozzle, the project's filaments. It may qualify that statement, and must, when the plain statement would mislead; the qualification is about the selection itself, comes from OrcaSlicer's own state, and holds regardless of what the chat says. The chip makes no claim about the physical machine: what is loaded, which plate is on, which nozzle is fitted, whether it is connected or busy. Those belong to the chat, the setup card's line annotations, the printer menu's first row, and the send dialog. The chat never changes the chip. (Kenneth, 2026-09-06, restated 2026-10-28: the September rule "the chip states facts and never warns" was about the chat steering the chip and about mismatches with the connected machine; it was not about the selection.) 9

11	- Every request carries about 10k input tokens (prompt plus 29 tool definitions); with `store:false` every tool call resends all of it plus the history.

The replies never answer the model's question, so it wandered 10–19 calls; about 150–200k tokens per run, 195–260M in total. The simulator runs (about 630, about 40M) and first-step runs (about 500, about 12M) were the cheap part.
13	- It began as a one-off shortcut, I kept it "for comparability", then chased its noise with more runs. The scripts logged no usage.

15	**Why:** the money, and the numbers were also bad: most unrequested slices came after about 15 empty reads, so the test partly provoked what it counted.

Use the stateful simulator (`run_workflow_tests.py`, `workflow_fixture.py`) and the committed first-step test (stops at the first tool call, 8-request cap). If more varied full conversations are needed, extend the simulator so replies answer what was asked.

content.text:
The most likely cause is JusPrin's own `slice_report` tool description, which tells the model that the slice findings "are Orca's own warnings and errors". I haven't proven this, because I didn't run any model: live tests need your approval first.

## Problem
The prompt already forbids this. It says tool results may say OrcaSlicer but "that is this app", and to speak in first person, never "OrcaSlicer warned". That wording is in the build you ran (953eddb355). The app doesn't save the requests it sends, so I checked the source at that commit and the saved chat, not the request itself.

The reply came right after `slice_report` and uses the short word three times: "Orca did flag", "Orca warns" and "Orca suggests". This is what the saved chat shows about where the word could come from:

| Where the model could read it | "Orca" | "OrcaSlicer" |
|---|---|---|
| System prompt | 0 | 2 |
| All 31 tool descriptions (test copy, `project_tools.json`) | 3 | 32 |
| `slice_report`'s result (the findings it was reporting) | 0 | 0 |
| The note in `slice_start`'s result | 0 | 1 |

- **Short word:** only three tool descriptions use it, and two are the slicing tools: [ToolRegistry.cpp:1417](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1417) and [ToolRegistry.cpp:1476](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1476).
- **Skills:** the only ones that mention Orca are print-issues and file-loaded, and nothing in this chat should have triggered them.
- **Rule's wording:** it only quotes the long name, and 17 of the 31 tools describe OrcaSlicer as if it were a separate program. A cheaper model may simply follow those descriptions.
- **Alternative I can't rule out:** the model may have shortened "OrcaSlicer" by itself.

## Tests and results
- **Existing tests:** they missed this, but they run on `deepseek-v4-flash`, and V4.1 appears nowhere in the test runner or its README. The `first-person` and `slice-warnings-ready` cases each passed 3 of 3 on V4 Flash, too few runs to catch an occasional slip.
- **Saved chats:** this is the only reply naming Orca, out of 31 with text: 1 of 3 on V4.1 Flash, 0 of 13 on Claude Haiku 5.5, and 0 of 15 with no model recorded. That's too few to compare models.

## Proposed test
Your global rule is not to fix a bug before reproducing it, and live runs need your approval, so that decision is yours. I recommend replaying the last request of this chat on `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`:
- **Runs:** 20 with the current wording and 20 with both names replaced by "the app" in the tool descriptions.
- **Cost:** each run stops at the reply, so that's 40 requests. At my rough estimate of 25k tokens each, that's about 1M tokens, and I'd report the actual usage.
- **What it tells us:** if the second set stops saying Orca, the wording change is the fix. If not, the tool descriptions aren't the cause, and the choice is between a stronger prompt rule and accepting this from the model.

Changing the wording without the replay is cheaper, but we wouldn't know whether it worked, since the slip may be occasional.

## Remaining issues
- **Collision warning:** "collisions may be caused" is in no saved tool result, though the app log shows the same warning. It probably reached the model through the workspace block, which isn't saved.
- **Test judge:** its question names "OrcaSlicer", and I haven't checked whether it would fail a reply that says only "Orca". The replay should count both words directly.
Did you find the original chat session?

Yes. The reply you pasted is saved in the project `p-695f6cbd7c153ebf-6d45f33818b087a0`, in the chat `c-2` titled "What Is on the Bed". The text matches, and the chat is recorded as `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` through OpenRouter, sent on 2026-10-30 at 13:58:52 UTC (06:58 on your Mac).

The file is `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/projects/p-695f6cbd7c153ebf-6d45f33818b087a0/current-state.json`. The reply is message `m-27`, the answer to the "The slice of Plate 1 finished." note.

That file holds the chat's messages, each tool call's arguments and the results as saved. It doesn't hold the requests sent to the model, so these are missing:
- the system prompt and tool descriptions as sent, which is why I checked them in the source at build 953eddb355
- the workspace block attached to each message, which is probably where the "collisions may be caused" warning came from

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build JusPrin translation catalogs from OrcaSlicer's .po files.

OrcaSlicer names itself in about 85 user-facing strings and in every
translation of them. Rather than editing those source strings (and the
translation macros) in upstream files, this script produces the catalogs the
application loads, with the product name substituted:

  * one <lang>/<domain>.mo per upstream .po, msgstr rewritten; entries whose
    msgstr is empty but whose msgid names the product get the substituted
    English text so the fallback also reads correctly;
  * an English catalog for the source strings in the .pot that name the
    product, so the untranslated UI switches too.

Attribution strings that must keep naming OrcaSlicer are excluded.
The .mo writer is self-contained so the build does not need gettext.
"""

import argparse
import re
import struct
import sys
from pathlib import Path

PRODUCT_PATTERN = re.compile(r"Orca ?Slicer")

# msgids that are attribution and must keep the upstream name.
KEEP_UPSTREAM_NAME = (
    "Open-source slicing stands on a tradition",
    "OrcaSlicer began in that same spirit",
    "Today, OrcaSlicer is the most widely used",
    "Orca Slicer is based on PrusaSlicer",
)


def unescape(s):
    return (s.replace(r"\n", "\n").replace(r"\t", "\t").replace(r"\"", '"').replace(r"\\", "\\"))


def parse_po(path):
    """Yield dicts with msgctxt, msgid, msgid_plural, msgstr (list), fuzzy."""
    entries, cur, field, fuzzy = [], {}, None, False
    for raw in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if line.startswith("#~"):
            continue  # obsolete
        if line.startswith("#"):
            if line.startswith("#,") and "fuzzy" in line:
                fuzzy = True
            continue
        if not line:
            if cur:
                cur["fuzzy"] = fuzzy
                entries.append(cur)
            cur, field, fuzzy = {}, None, False
            continue
        m = re.match(r'^(msgctxt|msgid_plural|msgid|msgstr(?:\[(\d+)\])?)\s+"(.*)"$', line)
        if m:
            key, idx, text = m.group(1), m.group(2), unescape(m.group(3))
            if key.startswith("msgstr"):
                cur.setdefault("msgstr", {})[int(idx or 0)] = text
                field = ("msgstr", int(idx or 0))
            else:
                cur[key] = text
                field = key
            continue
        m = re.match(r'^"(.*)"$', line)
        if m and field:
            text = unescape(m.group(1))
            if isinstance(field, tuple):
                cur["msgstr"][field[1]] += text
            else:
                cur[field] += text
    if cur:
        cur["fuzzy"] = fuzzy
        entries.append(cur)
    return entries


def substitute(text, product):
    return PRODUCT_PATTERN.sub(product, text)


def keep_upstream(msgid):
    return any(msgid.startswith(prefix) for prefix in KEEP_UPSTREAM_NAME)


def write_mo(path, messages, header):
    """messages: {key bytes: value bytes}. Standard GNU .mo layout, no hash table."""
    items = sorted(messages.items())

content.text:
No, I wouldn't do a blanket replace on the way to the model. Most of the "Orca" text the model reads is JusPrin's own English, which we can simply edit, and a replace would also corrupt real names. Translations need almost no new work, because the build already rebrands Orca's translated strings.

## Why not replace at send time
- **It breaks names the model has to send back.** Profiles include "Orca Arena X1 Carbon 0.4 nozzle" and "OrcaArena Generic ABS @base". If the model sees "JusPrin Arena…" and passes that to `printer_setup`, the preset won't be found. Matching only the exact word "OrcaSlicer" protects those, but not a person's file called "OrcaSlicer test.3mf".
- **It can make facts false.** The file-load report says which app saved a 3MF. A file saved by OrcaSlicer would then claim JusPrin saved it.
- **It covers up text we control.** In the saved chat, the only "OrcaSlicer" in a tool result was the `slice_start` note, which JusPrin wrote. The rest of that wording is in the prompt and tool descriptions, 35 mentions in the descriptions alone.

## What I'd do instead
1. **Reword our own strings:** the tool descriptions, the tool notes such as "OrcaSlicer's reason", and error messages such as "OrcaSlicer did not slice". Keep the prompt's one sentence saying that "OrcaSlicer" means this app, since real file data can still contain the name.
2. **Add a guard test:** fail the build if "Orca" appears in the tool descriptions or skills, as `wording.test.ts` already does for "arrive".
3. **Fix the bare word "Orca" in the catalogs:** see below.

## Translations
There are two kinds of text, and neither needs translating at send time:

| Text | Language | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| JusPrin's prompt, tool descriptions and notes | English only; the model already replies in the person's language | Edit the source |
| Orca's warnings and dialogs | Translated into 22 languages | Already rebranded at build time by [brand_catalogs.py](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Brand/brand_catalogs.py) |

The catalog builder has one gap: it only matches "OrcaSlicer" and "Orca Slicer", so the bare word survives. The built catalogs still have 27 entries with it in English, 25 in Simplified Chinese and 8 in Russian, including "Orca will automatically cap…", a warning both the person and the model can see.

Extending the pattern fixes every language at once, because translations nearly always keep the Latin spelling (the 22 languages keep it in most of the strings that name Orca). The ones I sampled that drop the name say "Studio" or leave it out, rather than spelling Orca differently. A few names need to be left alone or decided one by one, such as Orca Cloud and Orca Cube, so it should be a reviewed list and not a blanket replace.

## Limits
- **Stale catalogs:** `JusPrin2.mo` in your dev build is dated 2026-09-13, while `OrcaSlicer.mo` is from 10-28. The catalog target may not be re-running, so new strings could miss the rebrand. I also didn't confirm which catalog the running app loads.
- **This may not stop every slip:** I haven't shown that the wording causes it. A model could still say "JusPrin warned" instead of "I", though that's much less of a problem. The DeepSeek replay is what would show whether the rewording works.

You misunderstood what I mean. My understanding is that we have a listener to collect the error warnings and error messages orcaslicer fires, and we forward at least some of them to the model, probably as a structured input. What I mean is to replace by keyword matching before we put the raw messages into the structured input. I think this is what you mean here: Already rebranded at build time by brand_catalogs.py but I'm not a hundred percent sure.

You're right that there's a capture point, and I read your idea wrongly: you mean rewriting only the Orca messages as they're captured. I'll trace where those messages enter the structured input, and whether the catalog rebrand really does the same job.

content.text:
Your understanding is mostly right, and `brand_catalogs.py` gets a similar result by a different route. It doesn't match keywords on each message. At build time it rewrites the translation tables, so most of Orca's messages already say JusPrin by the time JusPrin captures them. Replacing at capture wouldn't have changed the reply you pasted, because none of the warnings the model received contained "Orca".

## Where Orca's messages get captured
There isn't one listener. These paths read Orca's text separately:

| Path | Where | Reaches the model as |
|---|---|---|
| Notifications, validation warnings, slicing-step warnings | [PrintIssueMonitor.cpp:232](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor.cpp:232), plus lines 413 and 438 | `sliceWarnings`, `<print_issue>` |
| Slicing-step warnings, read a second time | [OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2431](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2431) | `slice_report` findings |
| Dialogs during file load | [DialogListeners.cpp:120](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/DialogListeners.cpp:120) | The file-load report |

Keyword replacement would have to go in each of these, and in any path added later.

## Why the catalog is the better place
- **It doesn't touch names:** the translated text still has `%1%` where the object name goes. At capture, the name is already in the message, so an object called "Orca whale" would become "JusPrin whale".
- **The person and the model see the same words:** the warning chip uses the same text, so you don't need a second fix for it.
- **Translations are already handled:** each language's table is rewritten at build time, so there's nothing to look up at runtime.

## What's still missing
Of the 105 source strings that name Orca, 78 are rebranded in the built English catalog, because the builder only matches "OrcaSlicer" and "Orca Slicer". The other 27 are mostly cloud features, calibration test names, the About dialog and Preferences. These are the ones most likely to reach the model:
- **Four speed warnings:** "Orca will automatically cap…" for jerk, junction deviation, and print and travel acceleration.
- **Two setting descriptions:** both in `PrintConfig.cpp`, which `settings_search` can return.

I'd extend the builder with a reviewed exception list, keeping names like Orca Cloud and Orca Cube. The match should treat only ASCII letters as part of a word. Otherwise "Orca将" in Chinese wouldn't match, because the script's `\b` counts Chinese characters as word characters.

## What this means for the bug
The reply you pasted got "Orca" from somewhere else. The warnings it received were "It seems object root_1 has floating regions…" and "root_1 is too close to others…", with no product name. So the catalog fix is worth doing, but the likely cause of this reply is still JusPrin's own wording in the prompt and tool descriptions, which needs rewording either way.

## Corrections and limits
- **Stale catalog:** I raised this as a possible problem, but the English catalog contains all 105 current strings, so that worry doesn't hold for English. I didn't repeat this check for other languages.
- **Not tested in the app:** I read the code and the catalog files, but didn't trigger a warning in the running app. The code points to `JusPrin2.mo` as the catalog it loads.

def catalog_messages(entries, product, english):
    messages, header = {}, "Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8\n"
    for e in entries:
        msgid = e.get("msgid")
        if msgid is None or e.get("fuzzy"):
            continue
        if msgid == "":
            header = e.get("msgstr", {}).get(0, header)
            if "charset=" not in header:
                header += "Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8\n"
            continue
        names_product = bool(PRODUCT_PATTERN.search(msgid) or PRODUCT_PATTERN.search(e.get("msgid_plural", "")))
        msgstr = dict(e.get("msgstr", {}))
        if not any(msgstr.values()):
            if not (english or names_product):
                continue  # untranslated and nothing to substitute
            msgstr = {0: msgid}
            if "msgid_plural" in e:
                msgstr[1] = e["msgid_plural"]
        if not keep_upstream(msgid):
            msgstr = {i: substitute(t, product) for i, t in msgstr.items()}
        elif english:
            continue
        key = msgid
        if "msgctxt" in e:
            key = e["msgctxt"] + "\x04" + key
        if "msgid_plural" in e:
            key += "\0" + e["msgid_plural"]
            value = "\0".join(msgstr[i] for i in sorted(msgstr))
        else:
            value = msgstr.get(0, "")
        if value:
            messages[key.encode("utf-8")] = value.encode("utf-8")
    return messages, header


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--pot", required=True, type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--po-dir", required=True, type=Path, help="localization/i18n")
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", required=True, type=Path, help="resources/i18n")
    ap.add_argument("--domain", required=True, help="catalog file stem, the SLIC3R_APP_KEY")
    ap.add_argument("--product", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--stamp", type=Path)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    written = 0
    pot_entries = [e for e in parse_po(args.pot) if e.get("msgid")]
    for po in sorted(args.po_dir.glob("*/OrcaSlicer_*.po")):
        lang = po.parent.name
        entries = parse_po(po)
        messages, header = catalog_messages(entries, args.product, english=False)
        if lang == "en":
            en_messages, _ = catalog_messages(pot_entries, args.product, english=True)
            en_messages.update(messages)
            messages = en_messages
        write_mo(args.out_dir / lang / f"{args.domain}.mo", messages, header)
        written += 1
    if not (args.out_dir / "en" / f"{args.domain}.mo").exists():
        messages, header = catalog_messages(pot_entries, args.product, english=True)
        write_mo(args.out_dir / "en" / f"{args.domain}.mo", messages, header)
        written += 1
    if args.stamp:
        args.stamp.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.stamp.write_text(f"{written} catalogs\n")
    print(f"brand_catalogs: wrote {written} catalogs as {args.domain}.mo")
    return 0

          "tests/agent/test_mcp_protocol.cpp"]
SPECIAL = [("An OrcaSlicer editing tool is open, and OrcaSlicer does not", "An editing tool is open, and the app does not"),
           ("from OrcaSlicer's printer list", "from the printer list"),

SKIP_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*//|^\s*#include|\bthrow\b|BOOST_LOG|\b_L\(|TEST_CASE|SECTION\(")
LITERAL = re.compile(r'"(?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*"')
NAME = re.compile(r"\bOrca(?:Slicer)?(?:'s)?(?![A-Za-z])")


def reword(match):
    literal = match.group(0)
    for old, new in SPECIAL:
        literal = literal.replace(old, new)

    def one(found):
        word = "the app's" if found.group(0).endswith("'s") else "the app"
        before = literal[:found.start()]
        if before == '"' or before.endswith(". ") or before.endswith('\\"'):
            word = word[0].upper() + word[1:]
        return word

    return NAME.sub(one, literal)

import json,glob,os,re
for run in sorted(os.listdir('.')):

    if not reqs: continue
    seen=set(); stats=dict(reasoning=0,msgs=0)
    hits=[]

        b=json.load(open(r))
        for it in b.get('input') or b.get('messages') or []:
            key=json.dumps(it,sort_keys=True)[:4000]
            if key in seen: continue
            seen.add(key)
            t=it.get('type'); role=it.get('role')
            if t=='reasoning': stats['reasoning']+=1
            if role=='assistant' or t in('message','reasoning'):

No, not yet. The rewording and the catalog change are finished and pass their tests, but nothing is committed and two things are still open.

- **End-to-end check:** the build it needs, the app's test harness, is at step 589 of 782, and I'll run the check when it finishes.
- **Source of the "Orca" reply:** I don't have a proven answer. The saved chat and app log don't record the requests sent or DeepSeek's reasoning. My best explanation is below, and it's a hypothesis.

**What the logs and test runs show:**
- **The findings:** the warnings themselves didn't contain a product name, so they didn't supply the word "Orca".
- **Likely sources:** the `slice_report` tool description said "findings are Orca's own warnings and errors". It goes on every request. The print-issues skill, which fired at the start of that turn, also quoted "Orca will automatically cap". The system prompt only explains that "OrcaSlicer" means this app, so "Orca" alone went unexplained.
- **DeepSeek's habit:** in today's test runs on the older V4 Flash, 9 of 159 reasoning items name OrcaSlicer as the underlying program, but none of its 69 replies do.
- **Replay:** I rebuilt the final request and sent it to other models. `gpt-5.4-mini` named OrcaSlicer in 1 of 3 runs. `claude-opus-5-5` gave only one reply, which didn't name it, and called a tool in the other two runs.

**Correction:** I had concluded that no V4 run reached the warnings-after-a-slice situation, but that only holds for today's test runs. The prompt tests `first-person` and `slice-warnings-ready` do cover it on V4 Flash. They have two weaknesses:
- Each runs only 3 times, so an occasional slip could go unseen.
- `slice-warnings-ready` passes as soon as the model calls `slice_report`, without judging a reply.

V4.1 Flash, the model you used, has never been tested.

**Also unresolved:**
- One full Agent UI test run had a single failure, and I didn't capture which test. The next four runs passed, with 623 of 623 tests in the three I counted. Machine load was high, so it may be a flaky test, but I can't confirm that.
- `tests/project_prompt/requests.json` still has the old wording.
- `tests/project_prompt/baseline.json` needs a new live recording because the tool text changed.

To confirm the source, I'd need a live DeepSeek V4.1 Flash replay comparing the old and new wording: 20 runs each, stopping at the reply, roughly 1M input tokens in total. I won't run that without your approval, and I'll ask again in the final report once the end-to-end check is done.
